the presence of a templating agent in a complex mixture is sufficient to induce the self assembly of a supramolecular system.

the development of molecular systems able to selectively bind and to report the presence of specific molecules in a complex mixture.
the development of new molecular recognition systems able to selectively bind and report the presence of a specific guest molecule in complex media.
the design of new molecular architectures based on supramolecular chemistry and their applications to the development of molecular sensors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular systems are able to self-assemble in complex mixtures and that these systems can be used to detect the presence of a particular compound in the mixture.
the presence of a templating agent in complex mixtures can be exploited to drive self assembly and to selectively encapsulated specific molecules in the mixtures.
